title: Lab Notebook
intro: Our notebook records the construction, screening and validation of the astaxanthin and crocetin modules in Dunaliella salina from July to September 2026. The weekly account presents the experimental logic, while the complete dated record preserves procedures, observations, tables and supporting figures.

Dunaliella cell culture and pre-treatment (preparation stage)

Culture Dunaliella FACHB-435 under static conditions in modified PKS liquid/DM medium (containing 1.5 M NaCl) at 26 °C, 50 μmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹ irradiance, and a 16 h light/8 h dark photoperiod. When the cells reach the logarithmic growth phase (density ~10⁵–10⁶ cells/mL), the OD680 is approximately 0.5–1.0.
1. Harvest the log-phase cell culture and collect the pellet by centrifugation.
2. Discard the supernatant, resuspend the pellet in fresh PKS/DM medium, and wash the cells 3 times to thoroughly remove residual metabolites from the old medium.
3. Resuspend the washed Dunaliella cells in fresh medium and adjust the final cell concentration to 10⁶ cells/mL.
4. Transfer the cell suspension to fresh medium containing 1 M NaCl and continue culturing for 8 h. This step serves as “pre-adaptation” for the subsequent osmotic shock.
5. Take 1 mL of the pre-treated cell suspension, collect the cells by centrifugation, and discard the supernatant.
6. Immediately resuspend the pellet in fresh PKS/DM medium containing 0.1 M NaCl (still at a volume of 1 mL).
7. To this 1 mL suspension, precisely add, in order:
- Plasmid DNA: 5.46 μg of pCAMBIA1302 (the vector containing the target gene).
- Surfactant: 15 μL of 0.1% Triton X-100 stock solution (the final concentration assists membrane permeabilization).
8. Place the mixture on a vortex mixer and mix vigorously for 60–120 s (90 s recommended).
9. Immediately after vortexing, transfer the mixture to fresh liquid medium.
10. Recover under static conditions at 26 °C with 16 h light/day for 48 h. At this point, more than 90% of the viable transformed cells resume normal growth.
